I checked the mechanism's claims against the code. setup.sh line 8 has RUSTUP_VERSION=1.28.2, there are four per-platform sums, and line 24 refuses on a checksum mismatch. Line 29 is the exec of cargo run --quiet --locked --release -p xtask -- setup. Both tests that read this entry passed.

criteria.evidence: The file exists, and each property has its own test. the_spec_entry_names_the_setup_path_owner_and_test checks that every .sh/.rs/.toml token in the mechanism is a file. setup_sh_pins_rustup_and_checks_its_sha256 checks an exact version, four 64-hex sums, the pinned URL and the comparison with refusal. the_toolchain_channel_is_an_exact_version covers the channel. setup_sh_ends_in_one_locked_cargo_run checks there is one exec line, that it is the last command, and that it contains --locked and -p xtask and ends with `-- setup "$@"`. All 7 tests passed when I ran them.

findings.summary: xtask/shard-timings.txt changed but is not on the expected-deliverables list
findings.evidence: One line was added: `xtask --test setup_repeatable 5.00`. The change is needed because checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit (xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs:411) requires every test unit to appear in this file, and it was listed in the planned files. findings.summary: The xtask blanking case tests a local copy of the gap rule, not the real one
findings.evidence: blanking_the_mechanism_makes_the_entry_a_gap checks only that the file's own is_blank_or_none helper returns true for none, empty and None. That is close to a tautology, and it would not notice if the real spec_gaps rule drifted. The hestia.rs test does use the real spec_gaps, so the property is still shown. A simpler fix would be to drop the xtask case or point readers to the hestia test.

findings.summary: Several assertions are plain text searches that can give false results
findings.evidence: `assert!(!text.contains("latest"))` would fail if a harmless comment in setup.sh used the word 'latest'. `main.contains("already installed")` and `contains("fn gitleaks_present")` only show the strings exist, not that the steps skip when the tool is present. The accepted reading chose to read files rather than run setup, and the mechanism text says so openly, so this is acceptable. A unit test of gitleaks_present or install_sccache_at with a pre-installed fake binary would show idempotence directly.

summary: The change does what the request asked. OLY-B-RUN-02 in docs/spec.toml now names the existing one-command setup path as its mechanism: setup.sh hands off to `xtask setup` in xtask/src/main.rs. Owner stays Athena, and the measure names both new tests and ends `status: not shown`. I checked the mechanism's claims against setup.sh and xtask/src/main.rs, and they hold. I ran the new xtask test file (7/7 passed), the new hestia unit test (passed) and the existing spec test (30/30 passed). Athena's revert run shows the xtask test fails with the old `none` mechanism. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in the recorded CI run, and no governance file changed. Three minor findings, none blocking: xtask/shard-timings.txt changed although it is not a listed deliverable (the ci_shards test requires it); the xtask blanking case tests its own helper rather than the real gap rule (the hestia test covers that); and some assertions are plain text searches that can give false results.
